column1: # Domain|Priority|Phase|Parent issue|Provenance
@REF|P1|1|464|reference-research

Pin regional Saturn releases and timing profiles|Record release, region, revision and refresh-rate evidence; reject mixed-version fixtures; expose unresolved differences without choosing convenient defaults.; Correct coordination parent: Saturn #464, execution #477, begin research now (wave 1). Reuse accepted USA MK-81070 V1.003 and Japan T-14302G V1.000 locks from #467/#468/#473; Add platform clock/RTC/controller topology, BIOS/core/settings identities, measured timing domains and regional code/resource map. #492 measures timing/RNG, never silently coerce Japan/USA/PAL into the same 60 Hz profile; Existing CPK provenance has an unconfirmed PAL hypothesis only. Acquire no invented PAL reference, retain unknown and record exact evidence before regional attribution.

Index every Saturn campaign room and transition|Enumerate reachable rooms, entrances, exits and scripted events from the pinned game; attach captures; create one bounded child per observed room.; Cover every discovered Normal room/transition, solo and original co-op entry/exit, death/retry/continue/game-over, switches/puzzles/hazards, enemy/spawn waves, boss gates, bonus/secret routes, cutscenes/endings and progression flags; For each room join source bank/layout #484/#486, code consumers #480/#481, state #491, input-only route #490, save semantics #494 and Neptune comparison. Rendering tiles are not collision or objective logic; Track room/route/transition denominators by release, forced-state-only discoveries stay labelled. Generate bounded per-entity children #410, preserving unexplored branches instead of claiming completion after one traversal.

Index every Saturn enemy and boss phase|Record distinct actors, attacks, vulnerabilities and transitions; distinguish recolours from behaviour variants; create per-actor comparison tasks.; Inventory every discovered enemy variant, boss phase, mount/companion interaction and original CPU policy by mode/region, with transitions, decision cadence, RNG, hitboxes, damage/invulnerability and attack/projectile timing; Correlate natural repeated scenarios with code #483, state #491 and scheduling #492, include co-op target selection, simultaneous damage, interruption/death and rare-phase boundaries; Original battle CPU reconstruction feeds SATURN-014 (#430), Power CPU #505 remains separate. Enhanced Neptune bots must not be labelled faithful merely because they win or use the same names.

Index Saturn battle stages and hidden variants|Capture selection conditions, geometry, gimmicks and supported seats; test hidden-option claims; generate one task per confirmed variant.; Enumerate actual mode/settings/player/topology combinations: Normal/co-op, Master, standard and wide Battle, teams/rounds, timers/ties, sudden death, revenge/bonus/results and hidden options where observed; Measure controller/multitap mapping and original seat limits per mode, twelve-seat Neptune/Power support is not evidence for Saturn's original limits. Distinguish local battle from NetLink/XBAND #496; Link menu graph #495, transitions #490, rules #493 and source routines, record unavailable combinations and discovery evidence without treating advertised totals as exhaustive.

Inventory Saturn items and illnesses by mode|Record availability, stacking, caps, duration and removal in Normal, Battle and Master; retain counterexamples and unknowns.; Inventory every observed item, illness, bomb type, mount ability and mode-dependent effect across Normal/Battle/Master by release, identify source table/code and visual/audio resources; Specify acquisition, limits/stacks, timer refresh/expiry, persistence/death/reset, drop/spawn RNG, immunity/countereffects, kick/throw/mount and simultaneous-event interactions; Feed #407 per-game interaction experiments and #493 movement/bomb boundaries. Link exact source/state/units and generate separate disputed or unknown semantics tasks.

Inventory Saturn animation and sound states|Map movement, death, victory, carrying, mounts and campaign states to raw evidence; retain palettes, timing and missing-state records.; Enumerate all discovered players, enemies, bosses, mounts, objects, hazards, effects, menus/fonts/text, cutscenes, ending/credits, SFX/voices/music and palette/regional variants; Join #485–#489 and #495 to source bank/range, animation frames/durations/directions/anchors/layers, sound sample/sequence/trigger and runtime state coverage; Track extracted bytes, decoded files, reference reconstruction, private asset commit and Neptune presentation separately. No PNG/WAV count or lack of newly observed frames proves completeness.
@REF|P1|1|476|reference-research

Pin the current Power manual and settings inventory|Hash the developer-distributed manual and executable; enumerate every menu option and default; compare documentation with actual execution.; Coordinate under #476 and start wave 1. Pin developer-distributed client/server/manual and real hashes through #41/#498, identify VM/YYC and runtime/platform before choosing extractors; Inventory all actual menu/help/config/editor options, discovered mode names/settings and code/resource counts. Keep developer-advertised characters/stages/variants separate from measured denominators; Reconcile existing exports by bytes/resource IDs, do not assume their Power version from filenames or directory labels.

Inventory Power items and combination rules|Enumerate the pinned item-help entries and interactions; record mutually exclusive equipment and action priorities; split confirmed mechanics into bounded children.; Join observed item/bomb/illness/mount rules with #499 events/functions, #503 timers/RNG and #501 sounds/UI. Include stack/expiry, owner/collision, hazards, mode-specific overrides and simultaneous outcomes; Use full #407 interaction matrix per pinned Power release, retain unsupported instrumentation and uncertainty. Create bounded per-item/variant tasks from evidence, not guessed names.

Inventory Power stages and variant restrictions|Record every selectable variant, seat limit, mode constraint and hazard; distinguish advertised totals from measured entries; generate per-variant tasks.; Expand each discovered stage/variant with #502 room/layer/object data, procedural setup and event consumers, include collisions/spawns/hazards/wrap/elevation/sudden-death/settings/player eligibility where observed; Require a replayable local scenario and geometry/state comparison for each semantic family. Static texture extraction alone does not recover map behaviour or prove all variants.

Inventory Power characters and presentation metadata|Record animation requirements, portraits, palette variants and credits; distinguish cosmetic identity from mechanics; do not treat availability as redistribution permission.; Match every discovered character/resource ID to #500 texture pages, origins/masks, animation states/durations, variants, credits and source build; Separate cosmetic differences from actual ability/collision/gameplay code and aliases. #507 examines authoring/custom-data support without assuming existing mods imply a supported public API; Expand measured missing animation/variant cases idempotently, preserve exact duplicate aliases and unverified provenance rather than destructively deduplicating the repository.
@REF|P1|1|477|reference-research

Create a reference interaction experiment matrix|Cover item-item, bomb-hazard, mount-status and simultaneous-event pairs; prioritise high-risk combinations; retain replayable counterexamples.; Run independent Saturn and Power matrices as their inputs become available, completing both REF-005 and REF-008 inventories is not a prerequisite to a bounded single-game experiment. Catalogue mandatory dependencies become empty, each experiment declares its actual source contracts; Define factors for bomb/item/illness/mount/mode/terrain/player state, pairwise coverage plus targeted higher-order interactions, simultaneous event ordering and boundary sweeps; Compare code-derived predictions to repeated original runs via #493/#503, publish canonical input/expected-event traces, counterexamples and one-tick/one-unit mutants. Do not merge differing game semantics into one default.

Reconcile video claims with playable references|Catalogue claims and timestamps from the supplied video when retrievable; mark unavailable footage explicitly; verify gameplay claims against pinned builds.; Keep the supplied https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S1xMwFb_jGg as a discovery lead. Obtain actual accessible frames/transcript/timestamps before asserting contents, previous retrieval failure is not viewing; Map each evidenced mechanic/content/UI observation to exact release confidence and an existing/new deduplicated experiment. Footage timing and edits cannot substitute for pinned executable measurements; Use #509 primary-source registry, capture quotation/attribution and availability limits without uncontrolled scraping.

Maintain evidence confidence and coverage reports|Separate documented, observed, implemented and verified states; reject missing capture/build IDs; report gaps per release and feature family.; Connect #515's distinct static-byte/code/function/dynamic-target, route/mode, graphics/audio/map and behaviour ledgers to the current inventory and all new research jobs; Track unknown/hypothesis/observed/cross-checked status and separate decode/publication/Neptune parity evidence. Denominators can be unknown or expand, never call 100% of discovered entities total game completeness; Include reference release, source ranges, tool/core/settings, checkpoint/input, hash/evidence/asset commit, discrepancy and next experiment, preserve rejected hypotheses and forced-only states.

Generate bounded tasks from verified content inventories|Produce one idempotent child per observed entity/version; retain parent dependencies and evidence; never create invented assets or mark generated tasks complete.; Generate bounded children from verified entity/function/resource/variant IDs discovered by #477 research, including campaigns, co-op/Master/Battle, source-code modules and all asset categories; Deduplicate by game/release/source ID/semantic question, dry-run proposed issue edits, reconcile uncertain publication and preserve owner/active PR/history; Each child needs first slice, role/capabilities, dependencies, acceptance, real evidence and applicable gates. Maintain canonical issue links and close only evidenced acceptance, no speculative thousands of names.
@SIM|P1|1|43|neptune-requirement
Drive gameplay from an authoritative simulation clock|Represent durations in simulation ticks; pause and resume without wall-clock drift; compare outcomes across render rates and headless execution.
Partition seeded random streams by subsystem|Separate gameplay, bots, presentation and generation streams; serialise RNG state; prove cosmetic or planning queries cannot change item drops.
Define deterministic simultaneous-event ordering|Specify movement, pickups, placement, chains, damage and objectives in one tick; replay reversed input arrival orders; record stable tie outcomes.

Validate human and bot actions through one command path|Reject impossible movement, unavailable abilities and excess placements; return explicit rejection reasons; run equivalent human/bot action traces.

Implement fixed-point movement and corner assistance profiles|Measure subpixel steps and corner thresholds independently; test narrow corridors and opposed inputs; preserve profile-specific movement behaviour.
Specify tile occupancy and collision layers|Distinguish terrain, players, bombs, mounts and projectiles; test tile-edge rounding and overlap escape; publish consistent queries for bots and mods.
Implement spawn selection and safe spawn reservations|Reserve nonoverlapping supported spawn slots; detect insufficient reachable starts; reproduce seeded placement across clients and reconnects.
Make entity identities stable across snapshots|Use generation-safe IDs for actors and effects; reject stale references after despawn; preserve identity in replay and checkpoint restore.

Implement damage attribution and elimination events|Record owner, source, chain origin and assists separately; handle owner disconnect and simultaneous deaths; use events for results and bot diagnostics.
Define lives, hearts and invulnerability lifecycle|Specify hit, death, respawn, expiry and reset; test overlapping protection and repeated damage; keep mode and reference profiles separate.
Implement round start, countdown and clean reset|Block gameplay during countdown; clear transient entities and statuses between rounds; verify repeated rounds do not leak state or resources.

Resolve wins, draws and team elimination atomically|Handle simultaneous final hits and disconnected survivors; emit one terminal result; prevent duplicate rewards and delayed events changing a finished round.
Expose simulation snapshots and state hashes|Canonicalise state independently of dictionary order; include content locks and RNG; detect intentional divergence at the first differing tick.
Add bounded event queues and entity budgets|Reject recursive spawns and unbounded events deterministically; preserve authoritative state on failure; expose actionable pack/runtime diagnostics.
Version gameplay protocol and save schemas|Negotiate supported versions before play; reject incompatible peers and saves clearly; test explicit supported migration paths without silent fallback.

Implement pause and time-scale rules by session type|Permit local pause, define co-op consensus and online restrictions; keep timers and reconnect budgets consistent; prevent clients changing server time.
@BOMB|P1|2|43|reference-candidate
Specify normal bomb placement and owner overlap|Enforce capacity, grid snapping and placement cooldown; let overlapping actors leave once; reject re-entry and double placement in the same cell.
Specify fuse expiry and flame lifetime profiles|Measure fuse, growth and persistence independently; test exact boundary ticks; keep experimental timing separate from measured reference profiles.
Resolve multi-bomb chains and ownership|Handle simultaneous and multi-hop chains without duplicate damage; test insertion-order independence; preserve initial owner and chain attribution.

Define solid and destructible blast obstruction|Test directional stopping, destroyed-block ordering and hidden items; compare simultaneous blasts; make danger prediction use identical obstruction rules.
Implement bomb kicking and deliberate stopping|Test kick initiation, moving collisions and stop-at-grid behaviour; reject invalid stops; expose moving trajectories to clients and bots.
Implement pickup and carried-bomb lifecycle|Define pickup delay, ownership, fuse handling and cancellation; test carrier death/disconnect; prevent duplicate carried entities.

Implement throws, landing and chained bounces|Resolve occupied landings, wall contact and airborne shadow positions; test edge boundaries and simultaneous landings; preserve event timing across clients.
Implement wraparound bomb trajectories|Define entry/exit points and occupancy on wrapped maps; test corners and chained bounces; keep predictions consistent with authoritative landings.
Implement remote detonation ownership|Specify trigger ordering and owner death/disconnect policy; test remote bombs in chains; expose supported detonation actions to bots.
Implement penetrating power bombs|Define penetration through blocks and interaction with solid terrain; test mixed chains; compare real blast tiles with previews and hazard forecasts.
Implement rubber and bouncing bomb profiles|Specify bounce direction, speed, stopping and collision rules; test blocked loops and concurrent contacts; bound trajectory prediction.
Implement line-bomb placement|Place only allowed available bombs along valid cells; test obstacles, partial capacity and repeated inputs; apply one deterministic placement order.
Investigate bead or rolling-chain bomb mechanics|Capture the pinned reference before selecting semantics; prototype a separately named Neptune variant; test ownership, gaps and obstruction.
Implement landmine placement and triggering|Specify arming delay, visibility, activation and friendly-fire rules; test simultaneous crossings and chain reactions; expose truthful bot observations.
Investigate dangerous bomb fusion|Measure supported fusion pairs and blast geometry; reject unsupported combinations; test fusion ownership, capacity accounting and replay.
Implement bomb punch and aerial redirection|Define action range and target priority; test multiple bombs, walls and landing collisions; preserve authoritative action validation.
Implement bomb pushing and collision arbitration|Resolve actor/bomb and bomb/bomb displacement deterministically; reject impossible pushes; test narrow lanes and opposed actions.
Specify fire interactions with moving and carried bombs|Measure whether each supported bomb state chains, pauses or restarts fuses; test transition ticks; reject forecasts for unsupported states.

Implement bomb preview and placement feedback|Show capacity, supported trajectories and rejection reasons without leaking hidden information; match preview to authoritative rules; test controller and keyboard use.
@ITEM|P2|2|52|reference-candidate
Implement item pools and weighted hidden drops|Lock eligible items and weights per ruleset; use seeded server selection; prove clients and bots cannot inspect concealed drops.
Implement bomb-capacity upgrades and caps|Specify pickup, cap, reset and carried-bomb accounting; test repeated pickups and full inventory; preserve network and save round trips.
Implement fire-range upgrades and Full Fire|Keep normal and extended caps separate; prevent later pickups reducing range; verify actual blasts and full/minimal snapshots agree.
Implement skate upgrades and speed reduction items|Define discrete levels and profile-specific speed curves; test repeated reductions and cap boundaries; retain movement/collision consistency.
Implement kick, glove and line-bomb ability pickups|Grant capabilities independently of cosmetic characters; test death/reset and conflicting controls; expose supported actions to bots.

Implement heart and shield protection rules|Specify damage absorption and expiry; test simultaneous hits, crushing and mounted actors through explicit profile decisions; preserve HUD and replay state.
Implement temporary invincibility and flashing feedback|Define start/end ticks and damage exceptions; test expiry-edge collisions; offer reduced-flash presentation without changing gameplay.

Implement illness/status selection and transmission|Use declared status pools and seeded selection; test contact transmission, replacement and immunity; separate hidden random samples from observable bounds.
Implement short-fuse and long-fuse illnesses|Define fuse effects at placement and after pickup; preserve private randomness; compare real explosions with conservative bot forecasts.
Implement forced-planting and inability-to-plant illnesses|Bound automatic actions and enforce capacity; test death, pause and expiry; ensure client and bot inputs cannot bypass restrictions.
Implement slow, fast and reversed-control illnesses|Apply changes through validated movement/input semantics; test stacked expiry and control remapping; preserve reference-specific profiles.
Implement range/capacity restriction illnesses|Specify whether existing bombs change or only future placements; test pickup interaction and expiry restoration; reject invalid negative stats.

Implement illness cleansing and global Devil-style events|Define cleansing triggers, affected participants and event priority; test simultaneous pickup/contact; preserve deterministic global selection.
Implement item scatter and loss on damage|Specify which items drop, retention and pickup immunity; test mounts and simultaneous damage; preserve exact item accounting.
Implement item burn, relocation and respawn rules|Define fire destruction versus relocation per profile; test overlapping explosions and blocked destinations; prevent lost or duplicated items.
Implement score pickups and combo accounting|Separate score items from abilities; test pickup ownership and retry events; use permitted original art and explicit mode score tables.
Implement clock and time-stop effects|Specify affected actors and timers; test stacked pauses and expiry; keep network sessions and authoritative clocks consistent.
Implement block-pass and bomb-pass abilities|Define traversable entities and safe expiry when overlapping; test trapped termination and respawn; prevent unsupported bot routes.
Implement limited-use dash and movement abilities|Define charges, cooldowns and collision termination; test wall contact and control conflicts; publish movement traces for bot planning.
Implement item-slot action priority and selection|Resolve multiple active items on one input; provide explicit selection and HUD; test simultaneous pickup/use and controller remapping.
Implement pickup race and team sharing policies|Resolve same-tick claims and allowed sharing; test latency-independent outcomes; record personal/team ownership in snapshots.
Build item help and interactive demonstrations|Generate descriptions from versioned definitions; run small playable examples; show unsupported combinations and accessibility-friendly controls.
@MOUNT|P2|3|38|reference-candidate
Implement reusable mount and rider state|Separate actor, rider and ability state; test mounting, dismounting and owner death; serialise exact identity and collision semantics.
Implement eggs, hatching and growth progression|Define mode-specific growth inputs and maximum stage; test duplicate pickups and interrupted hatching; keep original and community profiles separate.
Implement blue Tirra-style bomb launch capability|Measure distance and growth effects before fidelity claims; test obstacles, landing and carried bombs; expose authoritative trajectories to bots.
Implement green Tirra-style dash capability|Define growth-dependent steering and stopping from evidence; test walls and sudden hazards; preserve rider input authority.
Implement yellow Tirra-style stun capability|Measure radius, targets and duration; test immunity and simultaneous roars; synchronise effects and readable warnings.
Implement pink Tirra-style jump capability|Measure traversable obstacle classes by growth; test landing occupancy and map edges; preserve shadow/hitbox separation.
Implement purple Tirra-style sonar capability|Measure reveal and detonation semantics; prevent unauthorised information reaching opponents; test hidden-item and remote-bomb interactions.
Implement mount damage and sacrifice lifecycle|Define rider protection, mount loss and post-hit windows; test chained hits and crushing separately; preserve exact death attribution.
Inventory Power Louie and other steed abilities|Enumerate pinned mounts and growth differences; create one child per confirmed ability; map each to supported public capability primitives.

Expose community-authored mounts through packs|Load original mount visuals and supported abilities without source branches; validate rider anchors and collision; reject unsupported bot/browser mechanics.
@ARENA|P2|2|35|neptune-requirement
Implement logical tile layers and visual themes|Separate terrain, collision, hazards and decoration; swap themes without changing state hashes; validate dimensions and layer references.
Implement normal and wide arena layouts|Support declared seats and readable camera framing; validate distinct reachable spawns; retain separate Saturn and Neptune capacity profiles.
Implement destructible block variants|Support health, drops and destruction events; test simultaneous blasts and state sync; keep material rules data-driven.
Implement conveyor belts|Define actor and bomb transport speeds and priorities; test intersections and blocked exits; expose timed movement to navigation.
Implement warp pads and teleport routing|Lock destination selection and occupancy policy; test loops and simultaneous arrivals; provide previews without leaking hidden routes.
Implement directional arrows and bomb curve tiles|Define which entities redirect and when; test loops and competing forces; keep forecast paths consistent with runtime.
Implement trampolines, launchers and seesaws|Specify activation, flight and landing rules; test multiple occupants and failed landings; support versioned hazard capabilities.
Implement rails, carts and moving platforms|Move riders and bombs through authoritative trajectories; test boarding, obstruction and disconnect; include motion in bot planning.
Implement doors, switches and rotating barriers|Define state transitions and actor occupancy during closing; test simultaneous triggers; persist puzzle state in saves.
Implement ice, water, lava and terrain effects|Treat terrain effects as declared capabilities; test overlapping statuses and movement; reject unsupported cross-platform or bot combinations.
Implement timed lasers, vents and floor traps|Expose warning/active/recovery phases; test exact activation boundaries; make authoritative hazard intervals available to bots.

Implement moving stage enemies and large obstacles|Use bounded authored actors with clear collision footprints; test occlusion/readability and multiple hits; distinguish stage hazards from competitive players.
Implement pressure-block patterns and warnings|Support authored and seeded pattern lists; test multi-block ticks, occupants and removed entities; retain warnings in reduced-effects presentation.
Implement collapsing floors and shrinking arenas|Define fall outcomes, refuge checks and progression; test disconnected actors and simultaneous collapse; preserve deterministic match completion.
Implement vertical layers and height restrictions|Specify traversal links, blast reach and landing rules; test stacked visual overlap; require explicit compatible bots and camera support.
Implement wraparound arena topology|Make adjacency, movement, blasts and camera cues agree; test all edges and corner transitions; validate graph connectivity.
Implement arena variants and deterministic presets|Share base geometry with explicit variant overrides; validate incompatible overrides; lock the resolved variant for replay and multiplayer.
Implement seeded procedural arena generation|Generate within declared fairness/connectivity constraints; reproduce seeds; reject unsatisfiable settings and preserve generation version.

Implement arena reachability and spawn fairness checks|Detect isolated starts, unreachable objectives and immediate forced deaths; report locations to authors; separate structural validity from competitive balance.
Implement hazard composition and event ordering|Exercise conveyor/warp/bomb and door/explosion combinations; define same-tick priority; reject loops that exceed declared budgets.
@BATTLE|P1|2|43|neptune-requirement
Implement configurable free-for-all survival|Support round count, win target, timer and draw policy; resolve simultaneous last eliminations; reproduce results from the command log.
Implement team survival and friendly-fire profiles|Support uneven and mixed human/bot teams; define shared victory and friendly-fire exceptions; prevent teammate information leaking to opponents.
Implement tile-conversion Reversi battles|Use the measured profile and existing #44 slice as the starting point; test tile ownership, ties and final scoring; expose objective progress to bots.

Implement Dodge-style avoidance battles|Pin reference victory and bomb restrictions before claiming parity; test survival and simultaneous eliminations; provide a separate original preset while measurements are missing.
Implement Hyper Bomber-style objective battles|Measure objective collection, delivery and elimination rules; test contested objectives and dropped progress; provide objective observations for bots.
Implement King-style scoring battles|Measure crown or target selection and scoring intervals; test transfer, ties and disconnects; keep score updates authoritative.

Implement Battle Royale rule profiles|Pin the reference meaning separately from modern genre assumptions; test its measured elimination and score rules; label an original Neptune interpretation explicitly.

Implement elimination revenge vehicles|Define perimeter movement, attacks and return conditions from the selected profile; test corners and same-tick revenge kills; support controller and bot actions.
Implement sudden-death and overtime options|Define ties, timer extensions and escalating hazards; test multiple overtime rounds; prevent indefinite matches with bounded policies.

Implement a configurable series and points table|Persist stage sequence and placements across rounds; test ties, substitutions and interrupted series; support an explicit long Saturn-style series preset after measurement.
Implement stage voting, shuffle and rotation|Use reproducible selection and published eligibility; handle empty pools and tied votes; lock the chosen stage before ready checks.
Implement starting loadouts and item bans|Validate per-player and shared settings against the selected profile; show rule differences before joining; reject illegal loadouts server-side.
Implement handicaps and asymmetric teams|Support explicit health, speed or equipment adjustments; mark adjusted sessions in results; prevent hidden competitive advantages.
Implement training matches and restart controls|Allow instant repeat of a seeded scenario with bots; retain settings and useful diagnostics; exclude practice from trusted competitive statistics.
Implement original capture-the-flag battles|Specify flag pickup, return, drop and simultaneous capture; teach bots both attack and defence; test team disconnect and overtime rules.
Implement original payload and zone-control battles|Provide bounded objective paths and occupancy scoring; test contested zones and stalled payloads; publish mode capabilities for authored variants.
@SATURN|P2|5|38|reference-candidate
Build Saturn Normal-mode campaign progression|Model measured stage ordering, exits and unlock conditions; preserve regional differences; run each confirmed transition through an executable fixture.
Build Saturn Normal-mode two-player rules|Measure joining, shared resources and failure conditions; test deaths and stage transitions together; retain separate Neptune co-op improvements.
Implement Saturn Master-mode stage progression|Measure stage sequence, timer and restart rules; test all confirmed transitions; keep Master state separate from campaign saves.
Implement Master-mode grading and score breakdown|Capture measured scoring factors and thresholds; reproduce known reference runs; display explainable category totals without guessed parity claims.

Implement campaign enemy spawning and room clear rules|Capture trigger, wave and respawn conditions; test leaving and revisiting rooms; create per-room children from the inventory rather than hardcoded assumptions.

Implement campaign bosses with explicit phase graphs|Build one confirmed boss as the framework example; test vulnerability windows and simultaneous hits; generate bounded phase tasks for remaining observed bosses.

Implement campaign cutscenes and transition timing|Separate skippable presentation from gameplay triggers; test skip, pause and co-op synchronisation; use independently authored placeholder media until permitted assets exist.
Implement campaign secrets and bonus entrances|Record evidenced entry conditions and rewards; test repeat visits and missed conditions; avoid undocumented secrets becoming mandatory progression.
Implement the Saturn bonus-game framework|Measure the crane/bonus inputs, timing and rewards; test player ordering and interruptions; keep reward decisions deterministic.
Implement Saturn battle setup options|Reconcile timer, shuffle, draw and Devil settings with pinned evidence; test combinations and defaults; retain a named versioned preset.

Implement Saturn hidden settings and selection gestures|Record exact observed controller/menu conditions; test false positives and discoverable alternatives; keep unavailable reference options visibly unverified.

Implement Saturn save, continue and game-over behaviour|Measure lives, continues and reset boundaries; test corrupted or incompatible saves safely; separate convenience autosave from faithful profiles.

Implement Saturn presentation and camera comparisons|Capture framing, HUD placements and animation cadence per supported resolution; compare screenshots at documented tolerances; distinguish art mismatch from rule mismatch.

Implement Saturn CPU behaviour comparison scenarios|Record observable decisions for the supported difficulty levels; compare routes and actions under matched situations; publish differences without calling enhanced bots faithful CPUs.
@POWER|P2|5|42|reference-candidate

Implement the pinned Power battle preset library|Translate measured defaults into versioned Neptune presets; test supported mode/stage/item combinations; report omitted or uncertain settings explicitly.
Implement Power Score-mode progression|Measure stage, score, failure and continuation rules; test transitions and submitted scores; isolate original substitute levels from reference claims.
Implement Power Turbo timing and progression|Measure the actual mode before selecting its semantics; test speed-dependent collision and control windows; publish comparable timing evidence.

Implement Power character-selection ergonomics|Support large searchable rosters, favourites and palette choices; keep installed compatible characters freely selectable; test missing packs and duplicate display names.

Implement Power taunts and battle expressions|Measure available actions and cooldown behaviour; implement original/licensed presentation through packs; keep mute and reduced-distraction options local.

Implement Power settings compatibility reports|Map each pinned setting to supported, partial or unsupported Neptune behaviour; show exact differences before loading a preset; verify mappings against executable tests.
@BOT|P0|1|30|neptune-requirement

Provide bots with an explicit public observation model|Expose visible actors, terrain and observable fuse bounds; hide concealed drops and secret sampled timers; test equivalent visibility for human and bot roles.

Predict space-time danger for all supported hazards|Combine chain reactions, moving bombs and stage hazards; compare intervals to actual simulation traces; reject unsupported hazard capabilities before a bot match starts.

Plan escape routes with travel and reaction time|Account for movement speed, turns and occupied tiles; test strict edge clearances and blocked refuges; retain a reproducible failure trace for every unsafe action.

Require a viable post-placement escape plan|Simulate hypothetical placement and changed chains; reject self-trapping actions; test that later input delay and shared occupancy can invalidate a stale plan.

Coordinate path reservations between team bots|Avoid head-on deadlocks and mutually blocked refuges; expire reservations after death or replanning; test congested corridors with mixed human teammates.
Plan destructible-block farming and item collection|Balance useful reachable drops against risk and travel cost; avoid knowing hidden item identities; test deterministic choices under equal utility.
Build opponent-trapping and tactical bomb planning|Evaluate exits, timing and opponent capabilities; preserve self-survival constraints; compare seeded duels against a documented baseline policy.

Teach bots kick, carry, throw and remote abilities|Select only actions supported by the observation/capability API; verify action execution and escape consequences; cover each ability with focused scenarios.
Teach bots mounts, terrain and stage mechanisms|Use declared movement links and hazard intervals; reject unsupported routes; test a mount ability and a moving-stage mechanism end to end.

Create difficulty profiles without hidden-information cheats|Vary reaction time, planning budget and mistakes explicitly; publish the profile parameters; test that all levels share the same observation permissions.
Create distinct and reproducible bot personalities|Separate aggression, item preference and team style from skill; seed personality variation; expose clear lobby descriptions and replay metadata.
Support companion follow, defend and assist commands|Validate player-issued role orders; avoid stealing critical puzzle actions or blocking humans; test command changes and disconnected leaders.

Support authored enemy perception and attack policies|Give campaign enemies bounded sensory and state-machine components; test spawn, patrol, chase and retreat; isolate enemy rules from competitive bot advantages.

Expose objectives to bots through a common interface|Represent capture, escort, collect and survive tasks with progress and legal actions; test two different modes; report unsupported objectives to authors.
Recover bots from stuck, oscillating and invalid paths|Detect lack of progress without teleporting or cheating; bound replans and fallback actions; retain the map/seed/decision trace for regression.
Budget bot planning across large rooms|Enforce per-tick CPU and query limits; degrade planning quality predictably under load; measure twelve-seat and supported stress profiles.

Build bot explanations and replay overlays|Show chosen target, danger interval and rejected alternatives in developer mode; preserve private-information boundaries for spectators; export concise failure evidence.

Build seeded bot tournaments and promotion thresholds|Compare survival, objective success, illegal actions and runtime across varied seeds; retain confidence intervals and regressions; block promotion on any safety regression.
@ROOM|P0|2|31|neptune-requirement
Implement twelve-seat extensible room capacity|Separate protocol capacity from reference preset limits; support mixed humans and bots; reject unsupported map/seat combinations before starting.
Implement local guest seats inside online rooms|Map multiple controllers on one client to distinct seats; handle device loss and guest names; test local guests alongside remote players and bots.
Implement host-controlled and automatic bot filling|Support empty-seat targets and difficulty choices; avoid replacing reserved reconnecting humans; persist the effective roster in match metadata.

Implement public and private room discovery|Filter region, mode, seats, latency and pack compatibility; keep private rooms out of public results; handle stale listings and full-room races; List compatible player-hosted servers with declared modes, required content digests and reachable endpoints, validate listing ownership and expire stale advertisements.
Implement invite codes and direct joins|Use expiring or revocable room capabilities; show compatibility before downloading content; test invalid, reused and full-room joins.

Implement ready checks with a frozen session contract|Lock rules, versions, packs and roster at countdown; invalidate readiness on relevant changes; reject clients with mismatched content hashes; Validate completed map, mode, item and selected-character downloads before readiness, refresh the session contract on pre-start roster or character changes and define safe boundaries for later changes.

Implement host transfer within a surviving server session|Transfer lobby administration and permissions; test leader disconnect and simultaneous claims; keep the authoritative simulation on its existing server.
Implement reconnect grace and seat reclaim|Resume authenticated seats without duplicate actors; retain bounded grace timers; test reconnect during countdown, death and round transition.
Implement human-to-bot takeover and handback|Define permitted takeover boundaries; preserve actor inventory and team; avoid two command owners during reconnect.

Implement spectator seats and admission rules|Support spectators independently of player capacity; enforce hidden-information and delay policies; handle joining mid-round and switching at round boundaries.
Implement rematches and persistent room settings|Retain compatible participants, packs and votes; clear transient match state; test players leaving during the rematch countdown.
